judgment: It is not I who seek the untaught child —
At the first casting, I tell.
A second, a third time is troubling;
if the child troubles me, then I do not tell.
It is good to hold firm.
image: A spring comes out under the mountain: Untaught.
So the noble one acts with decision
lines: it is good to use punishments —
to take off fetters and shackles.
But to go on with it brings shame.
If he takes the untaught in: good.
If he takes in a wife: good.
His son can keep the house.
She sees a man of gold
He is shut in, still untaught.
It is not good to be the raider;
it is good to fend raiders off.

notes.name_en: 蒙 is covered-over ignorance, the child not yet taught; 'Untaught', not Wilhelm's 'Youthful Folly'.
notes.L1: 刑人/桎梏: punishments as instruments that remove fetters — kept concrete, not moralised.
notes.L3: 金夫 a man of gold/metal (a rich or official man); 不有躬 'not her own'.
